verdicts.quote: exactly one user is created per data record, as one atomic unit: all appear or none do.
{ outcome: "created"|"rejected"|"failed", created_count: <n>, errors: [{ row, field, code, first_row? }] } ... `errors` is never truncated.
unique within the file compared case-insensitively (`duplicate_in_file`, also giving `first_row`); not already in the store, compared case-insensitively (`email_exists`).
No role column: created users take the host default role. Basis: a CSV must not be a privilege-escalation path.
the import page and the import request are available only to an authenticated identity the host authorizes as admin.
verdicts.missing: Whether bulk import is a distinct permission from creating a single user; the spec only says 'admin' and leaves the admin decision to the host (G-2).

verdicts.quote: header errors `missing_column`, `unknown_column`, `duplicate_column` (all of them listed, with row 1 and the column name...)
UTF-8 with an optional leading BOM that is stripped; comma delimiter; RFC 4180 double-quote quoting; LF or CRLF; first record is a header.
Partial failure and recovery: commit is atomic, so no partial state exists to repair
Over `MAX_FILE_BYTES` the upload is rejected with 413 `file_too_large` ... more than `MAX_DATA_ROWS` data records is rejected 400 `too_many_rows`
verdicts.missing: The actual values of MAX_FILE_BYTES and MAX_DATA_ROWS; the spec deliberately chooses none (G-1).

verdicts.quote: empty body part returns 400 `file_empty`; `email,name` + LF returns 400 `no_rows`; `email,name` / `z@example.com,Zed` with no final LF returns 201 with created_count 1.
a repeated upload of an already imported file is T-3 (all `email_exists`) with no change.
Synchronous completion, no job record. Basis: R-6's bound keeps the work to one request.
Outside this feature: no third-party or remote service is called; no outbound email.
how imported users first obtain credentials (invitation, reset link, none) and whether they are notified. This is a product decision for the user.
verdicts.missing: Whether created users are active or pending, whether they have a password, and how they first sign in.

verdicts.quote: Uploaded bytes live only in request memory (or a transient spool removed before the response is sent). Neither logs nor audit nor any other store retains them.
every import attempt, including denied ones, writes one audit record: event `user_import`, actor id, UTC timestamp, outcome
Timeout and cancellation: a client that disconnects mid-upload leaves no partial effect, because the write happens only after the full body is read and validated
verdicts.missing: Whether the admin can cancel an in-flight import from the page; retry is whole-file re-upload only, with no explicit cancel action.

verdicts.quote: unresolved. The requirement is that an import of `MAX_DATA_ROWS` rows completes within the host runtime's request time limit; neither value is known (G-1). No latency target is invented.
verdicts.missing: A concrete time bound; progress is only an indeterminate indicator (R-8) with no measurable progress.

verdicts.quote: Import only creates. It never changes or replaces an existing user.
verdicts.missing: That the existing single-user creation path keeps working unchanged is not stated.

verdicts.quote: formula-injection neutralization (values are stored verbatim after trim; any later CSV export owns that risk)
verdicts.missing: A maximum field length; name length is deferred to the unknown host model (G-3).
